result.topic_en: Pencil calculations for an initial-value problem in Riemann's gas-wave theory: initial data for x<0 and x>0 at t=0, an exponential ansatz for t in the variables p and q, and integration of an expression for x.
result.transcription:
Initial.
$x<0, t=0, x'=\text{const.}$ $\quad 0<x, t=0\quad x'=0$
$\varrho=\text{const.}$ $\quad \varrho=1$
$x'<a\log\varrho<-x'$
$t=e^{[-\alpha p+\beta q-]}$ $\quad t=e^{-p+q}\; e^{\alpha p-\frac{q}{\alpha}}$
$[-\beta\alpha\beta-]+\beta-\alpha=0$ $\quad$ [-$=e^{(\alpha-1)(p+\frac{q}{\alpha})}$-] $\quad x=$ a a
$([-\beta-]\alpha+1)([-\alpha-]\beta-1)=-1$ $\quad$ [-$t=p+q+\text{const}$-]
$p+\frac{q}{\alpha}=\frac{[-\ldots-]\log(t+\text{const})}{[-\ldots-]\;\alpha-1}+\text{const.}=\frac{\log((\alpha-1)[-\ldots-]t+1)}{\alpha-1}+b.$
$x=\int 2a\left(1-\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)\left(p+q+\frac12\right)\partial q+(-1+\alpha)\left(p+q-\frac12\right)\partial p\quad e^{(\alpha-1)(p+\frac{q}{\alpha})}$
[-$=2a(\alpha-1)\int(\ldots)$-] [-$\frac{q}{\alpha}$-] $+p$ $\quad =2a(p+q)\,e^{(\alpha-1)(p+\frac{q}{\alpha})}-\frac{\alpha+1}{2}e^{(\alpha-1)(p+\frac{q}{\alpha})}$
$\frac{1}{\alpha}\left(p+q\pm\frac12\right)\partial q+\left(p+q-\frac12\right)\partial p$
[-$\frac12\left(\frac{\partial q}{\alpha}+2\partial q+\alpha\,\partial p\right)$-]
$e^{(\alpha-1)(p+\frac{q}{\alpha})}$
$-\partial p-\partial q$
[-$(p+q-\frac12)\ldots$-] $\quad \pm\left(\frac{\alpha-1}{2}\right)\partial p+\left(\frac{\alpha-\frac12}{2}\right)\partial q$ [?]
$(\alpha-1)\partial p+\frac{\partial q}{\alpha}\;(p+q)\quad+\;(p+q)e$
$-\left(\frac{\alpha+1}{2}\right)\partial p-\frac{\alpha+1}{2\alpha}\partial q$

methods.what: Initial conditions for the problem: constant state for x<0, rest state with density 1 for x>0
Exponential ansatz for t in terms of characteristic-type variables p, q
Solving for the combination p+q/alpha as a logarithm of t
x as an integral of a differential form in p, q with exponential factor, and its evaluation
Result of the integration for x
